task/instruction.md, task/environment/Dockerfile, task/environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md, task/environment/instructions/integration.md, task/environment/assets/seed_data.json (fully parsed), task/solution/solve.sh, task/solution/app/src/db.js, task/solution/app/src/seed_data.json, task/task.toml artifacts line, task/tests/app_context.md, grep of all gates/scored judge.toml and prompt.md for seed facts
evidence:
PATHS: instruction.md:11 names /instructions/hireops_rules.md and /instructions/integration.md; instruction.md:13 names /assets/seed_data.json. All three exist under task/environment/ (instructions/hireops_rules.md 10780 B, instructions/integration.md 1090 B, assets/seed_data.json 28549 B). task/environment/Dockerfile:14-16 `COPY instructions/ /instructions/`, `COPY assets/ /assets/`, `chmod -R a+rX /instructions /assets`; the Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template Dockerfile (cmp). task.toml:2 artifacts = ["/app", "/assets"]. No other /assets or /instructions path is named in brief or notes (template placeholder notes.md correctly replaced by task notes).

CONTENT vs BRIEF/NOTES: seed parses as JSON. users: 10 accounts whose emails and roles exactly match instruction.md:17 (3 recruiter, 3 hiring_manager, 1 observer, 3 candidate); no password in seed (password comes from brief, as hireops_rules.md:11 states). jobs: 3 (hireops_rules.md:205 'three jobs'), each with recruiter_id, manager_id among hiring-manager accounts, interview_limit 3/2/3 (within 1-50). applications: 16, positions contiguous 1..n per (job,stage); the one REJECTED card APP-301 carries rejected_from=SCREEN and reject_reason (supports rules 3 reopen and 7 non-leak). stages list = Applied..Hired,Rejected matching rules:42-43. candidate_status_labels exactly matches the table at hireops_rules.md:182-189. thread_page_size=30 matching rules:144 and rules:208. messages: 127; APP-101 has 120 ('one conversation is long', rules:205), all sender_ids resolve, created_at strictly increasing with no duplicate timestamps per conversation so 'read_count counted from its first' (rules:206-207) is unambiguous. notes: 3, authors are a recruiter or the job's own manager. reads: 6 markers, each read_count <= message count.

CONTENT vs SOLUTION: task/solution/app/src/seed_data.json is byte-identical to the shipped asset (sha256 a1c65c80...7740 both; matches raw-evidence-index entry). solution/app/src/db.js:10-16,61-85 consumes every seed key (users, jobs, applications incl. rejected_from/reject_reason, messages, reads via read_count index, notes, stages, candidate_status_labels, thread_page_size), reads the file beside the module (rules:197-201), and uses role strings 'recruiter'/'hiring_manager'/'candidate' as seeded. solve.sh:35 copies app incl. seed into /app, consistent with instruction.md:15 (/assets unavailable at runtime).

CONTENT vs JUDGES: re-derived each seed-dependent claim. functional prompt.md:25 'the starting read markers give her [Lena] 1' -> APP-301 has 3 messages (REC3, CAN3, REC3), Lena read_count 2, third message by another sender => 1 unread: correct. app_context.md:29-30 'Noor Haddad's Platform Engineer conversation is long (120 messages at the start)' -> APP-101 JOB-PLAT 120: correct. functional judge.toml:317/326 30-message paging: matches thread_page_size and >30 messages exist. functional prompt.md:39 fallback 'his seeded Data Analyst conversation' -> APP-201 JOB-DATA belongs to Tomas: correct; Bill Okafor is JOB-DATA manager and Ingrid is not (judge.toml:362 access split holds in fallback too). polish judge.toml:32/41 use Noor's Platform Engineer conversation where Rafael is a recruiter: valid. visual prompt.md:14 'a seeded job with cards in several stages' -> JOB-PLAT has Applied/Screen/Interview/Offer: valid. K row (judge.toml:389) candidate non-leak is exercisable because seed contains notes, a rejection reason and rejected_from. app_context accounts list matches seed names/emails/roles. Judges otherwise use run-created jobs and say never rely on starting counts, so later state does not invalidate seed assumptions.

ADVERSARIAL: (a) Broken app that could pass this row's concern: an app that ignores read markers would show Lena 0 or 3 unread; the Z protocol reads her count before anything else, so the seed fact is actually exercised and would catch it. An app hardcoding sample data instead of loading the seed would lack the 120-message thread and fail the paging rows. (b) Conforming alternative that could fail: ordering messages by created_at vs file order gives the same order (timestamps strictly increasing), so no seed-ordering trap; a reasonable app interpreting read_count as 'messages read' yields Lena=1, consistent with the criterion. I found no seed fact a conforming app could read differently and be marked wrong.

LIMITS: I did not build the agent image or run Docker (not needed for this row; mechanical COPY presence is owned by check-assets-referenced.py / fixtures checks in the deterministic review). Raw-evidence-index scripted golden runs used the frozen seed bytes (hash match) but are not a configured judge run; this row's verdict rests on source/content reconciliation, not on any Oracle or judge score.
